classification.habit: Small, much-branched, spiny herb or subshrub
classification.habitat: Dry, arid to semi-arid habitats; often found in sandy or rocky ground
classification.distribution: Indian dry and semi-arid regions; species-level nomenclature should be checked against the current botanical treatment

identification.description: A low, highly branched and often spiny plant with small leaves and small flowers; exact species authentication is important because Fagonia nomenclature has changed across sources.
identification.whole_plant: Low, diffusely branched herb/subshrub with a wiry appearance and spines at nodes or leaf bases.
identification.root: Slender woody/fibrous root; pharmacognostic characters require authenticated specimen.
identification.stem: Much-branched, slender, green to brownish stems with spiny stipular structures.
identification.leaf: Small, opposite, compound/trifoliate-looking leaves with narrow leaflets; associated stipular spines are conspicuous.
identification.flower: Small solitary flowers, generally pinkish to purplish in commonly described Fagonia material.
identification.fruit: Small dry capsule, with mature fruit characters to be confirmed on authenticated material.
identification.seed: Small seeds enclosed within the dry fruit; detailed microscopy requires authenticated sample.
identification.bark: Not a useful primary macroscopic discriminator in the young herbaceous portions.

therapeutic_actions: Traditional use in skin and febrile disorders
therapeutics.precautions: Species authentication is particularly important because Fagonia names and accepted species concepts vary among references.
therapeutics.contraindications: No generic contraindication assigned here without formulation- and patient-specific evidence.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Fagonia species have been investigated experimentally for several biological activities, but this dossier does not translate such studies into independent clinical efficacy claims.
modern_information.safety_notes: Do not substitute a different Fagonia species solely on the basis of a common name. Verify botanical identity before medicinal use.
